name: @bananaworld/design-system
description: Shared Bananaworld design system + shared pure logic used by both Bananaworld-DC and Bananaworld-CRM. The UI barrel ('.') is the 28 pure UI primitives + per-surface (data-surface) tokens — pure presentation only: no network, no permission/scope logic (TECH-COMP-003 / ADR-001). A separate './pricing' subpath ships THE single shared price-calculation engine (pure, no IO — CRM ADR-007 / PRD-FUNC-060) so a quote and the eventual order price identically; it never imports the UI layer. Shipped as TypeScript source; consumers transpile it via Next.js transpilePackages.

pnpm.//overrides: nanoid — TWO high advisories (GHSA-28wg-ghj8-5hjv <3.3.16, GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8 <3.3.18; both are infinite-loop DoS on a nonsensical size, no disclosure) reach the prod closure by ONE path: the auto-installed `next` PEER > postcss@8.4.31 > nanoid@3.3.12. They were published after this repo was last touched, so they fail the Dependency Audit on EVERY pull request here, including one that changes nothing. OVERRIDDEN RATHER THAN IGNORED, deliberately: bananaworld-dc met the identical advisory first and resolved it this way (a20cf381, PR #160, 2026-08-08), and the standing next-peer ignore above records its own revisit trigger as "when the estate advisory batch bumps next" — which is this. An ignore here would book a 7th standing exception at the exact moment the 6th said to stop. ^3.3.17 resolves 3.3.18 and clears both. Owner CHOSE this over extending ignoreGhsas, in writing, at the CR-DESIGN-SYSTEM-002 decision gate on 2026-08-14 (D-12). No Hard Rule 2 citation belongs here and its absence is the point: an override trades nothing away, so unlike the ignores below it is a fix and not an exception. Verified by running: `pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=high` exits 1 without this and 0 with it; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes, so the lock and manifest agree.
pnpm.//auditConfig: GHSA-f88m-g3jw-g9cj (sharp <0.35.0, libvips CVEs) reaches this package ONLY through the `next` PEER dependency that pnpm auto-installs so tsc can typecheck. This library ships TypeScript source only (files:["src"]) and no sharp; consumer apps (Bananaworld-DC / -CRM) provide and patch their own next+sharp. Ignored so `pnpm audit --prod` reflects what this library actually ships, not a peer's transitive tree. Revisit if next/sharp ever move out of peerDependencies. Owner-approved 2026-07-22 (Hard Rule 2, in writing).
pnpm.//auditConfig-next-peer: The five next/postcss advisories below (Next.js DoS GHSA-m99w-x7hq-7vfj + SSRF GHSA-89xv-2m56-2m9x / GHSA-p9j2-gv94-2wf4; PostCSS file-read GHSA-6g55-p6wh-862q + source-map path-traversal GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849) reach this package ONLY through that same auto-installed `next` PEER (audit paths `.>next`, `.>next>postcss`); next@15.5.19 / postcss@8.4.31 are identical to origin/main and to the estate's other repos, and this library ships none of that code. Same basis as the sharp ignore above. Owner-approved 2026-07-26 (Hard Rule 2, in writing) as part of GL-204 MS-1. Revisit when the estate advisory batch bumps next, or if next moves out of peerDependencies.
